text: GlideDialogWindow and GlideModal are the two real client-side APIs ServiceNow gives you for interrupting a user with a popup before they move on. Both are called from a Client Script or from a UI Action's client-side script — never from server-side code — and both exist so you don't have to hand-build a custom popup out of raw DOM every time you need to pause the user for a decision.

GlideModal is the lighter of the two. You create a new GlideModal, give it a title, optionally set a preference like a message string using setPreference, and call render. That's the entire pattern for a simple confirmation or warning — no custom UI Page required, because ServiceNow ships built-in UI Pages like glide_modal_confirm specifically for this case.

GlideDialogWindow is heavier and more capable. You pass its constructor the name of an existing UI Page — here, close_reason_dialog from Chapter 4's lab — set a title, and use setPreference to pass data into that page. In this example, the current record's sys_id and a task count travel in through setPreference, then calling render displays the UI Page's own fields and client script inside the modal overlay.

The real decision is always the same question: does this need a custom UI Page's interactive content, or just a message? A one-line delete confirmation is GlideModal — building and maintaining a whole UI Page for it would be unnecessary overhead. A dialog where the user has to pick a close code from a list, type a reason, and review which records will be affected needs real form fields, which means it needs its own UI Page, which means GlideDialogWindow is the only API that fits.

Get this decision backwards in either direction and you pay for it. Reaching for GlideDialogWindow when GlideModal would do means an extra UI Page record to maintain for something that was always just a sentence. Reaching for GlideModal when you actually need custom fields means fighting an API that was never built to hold that much content. Next up: UI Scripts — reusable client-side JavaScript libraries you can share across every Client Script, UI Page, and dialog in your application.
